name: Element Suppression
body:
School transmutation [void]; Level psychic 8, shaman 8, sorcerer/wizard 8

Casting Time 1 standard action

Components V, S, DF

Range medium (100 ft. + 10 ft./level)

Target one creature

Duration permanent

Saving Throw see text; Spell Resistance yes

Void: Spells with this descriptor are tied with a philosophical school of magic based on a concept known as the Void. The school teaches that the Void is the nothingness from which springs forth creativity, insight, spirit, thought, and also the source of pure energy from which all elements and phenomena are derived. Channeling the power of the Void (or the Void element) allows for the manipulation of the elements in objects and creatures, among other possibilities. Spells with the void descriptor are considered to belong to the Void element (for geomancers) and the void elemental school (for void elementalists).

If a spell has the [void] descriptor, it cannot be dispelled by elements release regardless of how high is your CL.

Void is the unifying element and force that binds all other elements together.

Those who can manipulate Void can leverage it to cause great disorder in the elements within a creature, such as with this spell. This spell manipulates one of the elements in a target, forcibly weakening it to the minimum necessary to maintain the target’s life.

When you cast this spell, you must choose one of the following elements in the target to affect, applying the associated penalties on the target as shown on the table below.

Element Effect Save Blood Wisdom reduced to 1, -6 penalty to Fort saves Will Earth Constitution reduced to 1, -6 penalty to Will saves Fort Fire Intelligence reduced to 1, -6 penalty to Ref saves Ref Water Strength reduced to 1, -6 penalty to Will saves Will Wood Dexterity reduced to 1, -6 penalty to Fort saves Ref Void Charisma reduced to 1, lose all ki points and cannot gain or replenish ki points Fort Characters may lose the ability to cast spells or use certain abilities due to failing to meet the minimum ability score required, depending on their class. The target remains in this state until a heal, limited wish, miracle, or wish spell is used to cancel the effects. Even though this spell applies penalties similar to bestow curse, it is not a curse effect.
